motion.name: reveal-rise
motion.value: transform: translateY(1.15rem) -> none; 550ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1); delay calc(var(--i, 0) * 80ms)
motion.purpose: Programme unfolding: dated rows assemble on scroll. Transform-only; gated by html.home-motion; observer rootMargin 0 0 -8%, threshold 0.15; --i capped at 4.

motion.name: fold-open
motion.purpose: At a glance / Full programme fold on entry rows.

motion.name: state-swap
motion.value: 160ms ease-out on color / background-color / border-color / text-decoration-color
motion.purpose: All hover and state changes on controls and links.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables reveal transforms, transitions, smooth scroll, and the stamp rotation
motion.purpose: Content is visible by default; JS never hides information.

themeMirror.note: Light and dark are set in one scoped block per press (body[data-page="home"], html[data-theme="dark"] override, and the prefers-color-scheme fallback). Meta theme-color tracks the press via window.THEME_COLORS consumed by site.js.

narrative.overview: The home page is the programme document of one working practice — the printed booklet itself, not a poster about it. Everything on the surface speaks that world's native material: rules and folios, a numbered running order of works, dated notices, a rubber-stamped issue line, a full-bleed box-office band with hatch texture. The paper is cool bone, the ink is near-black printer ink, and exactly one saturated colour — ticket red — carries every mark that matters. The visitor reads identity first (the name set as the season title), then proof of liveness (a real "Programme issued" timestamp fed by the content API), then the running order, then the notices, then the booking window. Nothing is centered-trio hero furniture; nothing is a row of equal cards. Depth is letterpress, never lighting: rules from 1px hairlines to a 4px masthead underline, a double red border+outline on the issued stamp, a diagonal hatch band, and one small shadow under the stamp. There are no gradients, no glass, no rounded surfaces. Motion is the programme unfolding as you scroll — dated rows rise into place, one named control ("At a glance" / "Full programme") opens or closes the running order — and all content is visible by default without JS or under reduced motion. The system currently ships on the home page only; other pages still render the previous cream+Playfair binding until adopted, and that legacy world is not part of this system.
keyCharacteristics: Bone paper ground, printer-ink text, one ticket-red accent at folio scale plus (at most) one full-bleed red band.
Fixed typographic scale ladder — folio, body, entry, name — with all display type set uppercase in condensed Barlow.
Letterpress structure: rules, double borders, hatch texture, one stamp shadow; zero gradients, zero glass, zero rounded surfaces.
Live data as identity furniture: the issued stamp and dated notices render real timestamps; the world never fabricates a date.
Two presses of one ink: every light token has a dark mirror; switching theme is switching print run, not switching design.

rules.name: The Ticket Red Rule
rules.body: Ticket red is the system's only voice of emphasis — no second accent, no gradient to fake a second one. At rest it appears only as folio-scale marks; exactly one full-bleed band per page may invert it into a surface. Its rarity is the point: when red appears on a new surface, it must mean something (a folio, a live mark, a booking action).

rules.name: The Two Presses Rule
rules.body: Light and dark are one system printed twice: every token has a mirror value, set together in the same scoped block. Never hardcode one press.

rules.name: The Fixed Ladder Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from the four-step ladder (folio, body, entry, name) before any invented size. One-off variants exist only as documented furniture steps; a new surface reaches for the ladder first.

rules.name: The Set-Caps Rule
rules.body: Programme words in the display face are uppercase and tracked; only the δ glyph and real date strings break caps. Never set body prose in Barlow.

rules.name: The Bleed Rule
rules.body: Full-bleed elements reach the viewport edge only via the −7.5% counter-offset of the column gutter, so the band's content realigns with the page column.

rules.name: The Pressed, Not Lit Rule
rules.body: Convey depth with rules, double borders, hatch texture, and the one stamp lift — never with shadows-as-lighting, gradients, or blur. If a new surface needs to feel raised, give it the stamp's paper (#f1eee5 / #1f221b) and a border, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Real Dates Rule
rules.body: The issued stamp, notice dates, and masthead latest-notice line always render live content from the APIs; furniture with no real data stays hidden. The stamp's credibility is the whole world's credibility.

dos: Do adopt the world on a new page by remapping the shared token names in one scoped block (as body[data-page="home"] does), light and dark together — the shared chrome then inherits the world for free.
Do keep every token pair dual-press: light value plus dark mirror, written in the same block.
Do set display type uppercase Barlow Condensed from the fixed ladder; track small settings (0.12–0.2em) and leave large settings near 0.
Do render the issued stamp, notice dates, and nav labels from the live APIs; hide furniture that has no real data.
Do use the stamp lift only on the stamp; use borders, hairlines, and hatch for everything else.
Do keep reveal transforms and 160ms colour state swaps; ship content visible without JS.
donts: Don't mix worlds inside one page: a page either carries the Season Programme remap or stays explicitly legacy — never a legacy cream/Playfair element beside this world's bone/Barlow.
Don't add a second saturated accent, a gradient, or a glass/blur surface; this world is paper, ink, rules, and one red.
Don't invent kickers, eyebrows, boxed glyph icons, or hard offset shadows; the only glyph furniture is text itself (δ, ↗, ↓) set in the system's own faces.
Don't fabricate dates, issue stamps, or programme data — the stamp's credibility is the whole world's credibility.
Don't round world surfaces: 0px corners on new components; the 2px chrome micro-radius is inherited legacy, not invitation.
Don't soften box-office copy below full paper (#eae7de / #191b16 ink equivalent) on red; that was a shipped fix, keep it.
Don't animate opacity of informative content; reveal is transform-only.
